complexor_blend.document: A manufacturer needs to create exactly 1 kilogram of a special alloy blend. Two alloys are available: Alloy 0 costs $10 per kg and Alloy 1 costs $20 per kg. The target blend must contain exactly 50% of Element A and exactly 50% of Element B. Alloy 0 is composed of 50% Element A and 10% Element B. Alloy 1 is composed of 50% Element A and 90% Element B. How much of each alloy should be purchased to minimize total cost?

complexor_diet.document: A nutritionist is planning a daily diet using Apples and Bananas. Apples cost $2.00 each and Bananas cost $1.50 each. The diet must provide between 50 and 100 units of Vitamin C, and between 30 and 60 units of Fiber. Each Apple provides 10 units of Vitamin C and 5 units of Fiber. Each Banana provides 5 units of Vitamin C and 10 units of Fiber. At most 10 of each food may be purchased. What is the minimum-cost diet that satisfies all nutritional requirements?

complexor_dietu.document: A dietitian is planning meals using three foods. Food 1 costs $2.00/unit, Food 2 costs $3.00/unit, and Food 3 costs $1.50/unit. Food 1 provides 2 units of Nutrient A and 3 of Nutrient B per unit. Food 2 provides 1 unit of Nutrient A and 4 of Nutrient B per unit. Food 3 provides 3 units of Nutrient A and 2 of Nutrient B per unit. The diet must provide between 50 and 200 units of Nutrient A, and between 60 and 250 of Nutrient B. Up to 100 units of each food may be purchased. Minimize cost while meeting all nutritional bounds.

complexor_knapsack.document: You are packing a hiking bag with a maximum weight capacity of 50 kg. Three items are available: Item 1 weighs 10 kg and has a value of $60. Item 2 weighs 20 kg and has a value of $100. Item 3 weighs 30 kg and has a value of $120. Each item is either fully packed (1) or left out (0) — no fractions. Which items should you pack to maximize total value without exceeding the weight limit?

complexor_media.document: An advertising agency must cover 3 audience groups at minimum cost. Three channels are available: Channel 0 costs $10 and reaches Audiences 0 and 1. Channel 1 costs $15 and reaches Audiences 1 and 2. Channel 2 costs $20 and reaches Audiences 0 and 2. Each audience must be reached by at least one selected channel. Each channel is either selected (1) or not (0). What is the cheapest selection of channels that covers all audiences?

complexor_cell_tower.document: A telecom company wants to build cell towers to cover as many people as possible. Two potential tower sites are available: Tower 0 costs 3000000 dollars and covers Region 0 (population 100) and Region 2 (population 150). Tower 1 costs 4000000 dollars and covers Region 1 (population 200). The total construction budget is 4000000 dollars. Each tower is either built (1) or not (0). Which towers should be built to maximize the total covered population?

complexor_cutting.document: A paper manufacturer cuts rolls of width 10 units to fulfill customer orders. Orders require: 4 pieces of 2-unit width, 2 pieces of 3-unit width, and 2 pieces of 5-unit width. Two cutting patterns exist: Pattern A: cuts 1 piece of 2-unit and 2 pieces of 3-unit from one roll (8 units used). Pattern B: cuts 1 piece of 5-unit from one roll (5 units used). The number of rolls cut must be a whole number. Decide how many rolls to cut with each pattern to fulfill all orders using the fewest raw rolls.

complexor_transport.document: A logistics company ships goods from 2 warehouses to 2 customers. Warehouse 1 has 20 units of supply and Warehouse 2 has 30 units. Customer 1 needs exactly 30 units and Customer 2 needs exactly 20 units. Shipping costs per unit: W1 to C1 is $8, W1 to C2 is $6, W2 to C1 is $5, W2 to C2 is $10. Route capacity limits: W1 to C1 at most 15, W1 to C2 at most 25, W2 to C1 at most 25, W2 to C2 at most 20. Minimize total shipping cost while meeting all supply and demand.

complexor_steel.document: A steel plant produces two products: Product 1 and Product 2. Product 1 earns $10 profit per ton, Product 2 earns $20 per ton. Production passes through two stages. Stage 1 has 10 hours per week; Product 1 uses 2 hours per ton and Product 2 uses 3 hours per ton in Stage 1. Stage 2 has 8 hours per week; Product 1 uses 3 hours per ton and Product 2 uses 2 hours per ton in Stage 2. Contracts require at least 1 ton of Product 1 and at least 2 tons of Product 2 per week. Market limits production to at most 5 tons of Product 1 and 4 tons of Product 2. How many tons of each product should be produced to maximize weekly profit?

complexor_prod.document: A factory produces three product types sharing a single resource pool of 4 units capacity. Product 1 earns $5 profit per unit and consumes 1/3 resource units per unit produced (max 4 units). Product 2 earns $10 profit per unit and consumes 1 resource unit per unit produced (max 6 units). Product 3 earns $8 profit per unit and consumes 1/2 resource unit per unit produced (max 3 units). Maximize total profit subject to the resource limit and production bounds.

complexor_revenue.document: An airline sells two flight packages. Package 1 earns $100 per ticket and uses seats on Flight Legs 1 and 2. Package 2 earns $150 per ticket and uses seats on Flight Legs 2 and 3. Flight Leg 1 has 50 seats, Flight Leg 2 has 60 seats, and Flight Leg 3 has 70 seats. Market demand limits: at most 30 tickets for Package 1 and 40 tickets for Package 2. How many tickets of each package should be sold to maximize total revenue?

complexor_aircraft_assign.document: An airline assigns 3 aircraft types to 2 routes to meet demand at minimum cost. Aircraft 0 is available at most 2 times, Aircraft 1 at most 3 times, Aircraft 2 at most 1 time. Route 1 needs at least 100 passenger-seats total and Route 2 needs at least 150. Seats per deployment: Aircraft 0 provides 50 on Route 1, 70 on Route 2; Aircraft 1 provides 60 on Route 1, 80 on Route 2; Aircraft 2 provides 70 on Route 1, 90 on Route 2. Costs per deployment: Aircraft 0 costs $100 for Route 1, $200 for Route 2; Aircraft 1 costs $150 for Route 1, $250 for Route 2; Aircraft 2 costs $200 for Route 1, $300 for Route 2. How many times should each aircraft be assigned to each route to minimize total cost? The number of deployments must be a whole number.

complexor_aircraft_land.document: An airport schedules landing times for 3 aircraft to minimize total penalty. Aircraft 1: earliest landing time 1, latest 10, target 4; penalty $5/minute early, $10/minute late. Aircraft 2: earliest 3, latest 12, target 8; penalty $10 early, $20 late per minute. Aircraft 3: earliest 5, latest 15, target 14; penalty $15 early, $30 late per minute. Minimum separation between landings: at least 2 minutes between Aircraft 1 and 2, 3 minutes between Aircraft 1 and 3, 4 minutes between Aircraft 2 and 3. Aircraft land in order 1, 2, 3. Assign landing times to minimize total penalties.

complexor_car.document: An event organizer assigns 3 participants to 3 cars. Feasible assignments: P1 can receive C1 or C3; P2 can only receive C2; P3 can receive any car. Each participant receives at most one car; each car goes to at most one participant. All assignment decisions are binary. Maximize the total number of successful assignments.

const_declarations.description: C1 to at most one participant
C2 to at most one participant
C3 to at most one participant

complexor_multi.document: A distributor ships two products between 2 origins and 2 destinations. Origin 1 supplies 20 units of Product 1 and 30 units of Product 2. Origin 2 supplies 40 units of Product 1 and 10 units of Product 2. Destination 1 needs exactly 30 units of each product; Destination 2 needs 30 of Product 1 and 10 of Product 2. Total shipment (both products combined) limits per corridor: O1-D1 max 35, O1-D2 max 25, O2-D1 max 20, O2-D2 max 30. Costs per unit: O1-D1 P1=$2, O1-D1 P2=$3, O1-D2 P1=$4, O1-D2 P2=$1, O2-D1 P1=$3, O2-D1 P2=$2, O2-D2 P1=$2, O2-D2 P2=$4. Minimize total shipping cost.

complexor_netasgn.document: A manager assigns work hours from 2 employees to 2 projects to minimize cost. Employee 1 has exactly 8 hours to allocate; Employee 2 has exactly 7 hours. Project 1 requires exactly 5 hours of work; Project 2 requires exactly 10 hours. Hourly costs: E1 on P1=$10, E1 on P2=$20, E2 on P1=$15, E2 on P2=$25. Hour limits: E1 can contribute at most 5 hours to P1 and 6 to P2; E2 can contribute at most 4 hours to P1 and 7 to P2. All employee hours must be fully used. Minimize total cost.

complexor_flowshop.document: A factory schedules 3 jobs through 2 machines in sequence (every job goes through Machine 1 then Machine 2). Processing times: Job 1 takes 1 hour on Machine 1 and 3 hours on Machine 2; Job 2 takes 2 hours on Machine 1 and 2 hours on Machine 2; Job 3 takes 3 hours on Machine 1 and 1 hour on Machine 2. Each machine processes one job at a time. A job cannot start on Machine 2 until it finishes on Machine 1. Find the job sequence that minimizes total completion time (makespan).

const_declarations.description: each slot has exactly one job
each job assigned to one slot
slot s+1 starts after slot s finishes on machine m

complexor_netmcol.document: A shipping company transports Product 1 from City A to City B. City A has exactly 10 units of Product 1 to ship; City B needs exactly 10 units. The route costs $1 per unit. The link can carry at most 10 units of Product 1, and the joint capacity on this link is also 10 units. How many units should be shipped to minimize total cost?
